questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to study abroad. And I wanted it to be somewhere far away so that I could truly experience feeling independent. Australia specifically has alway fascinated me in that it is a western culture that is isolated so far away from anywhere else. Their nature and wildlife were truly some of the most amazing I have ever seen as it is so different from anything else I have ever experienced. Furthermore the academic level of the universities in Australia is very high, so I feel it allowed me to develop myself intelectually. Lastly, it was bonus that Australia is an English-speaking country, so that I really got a chance to develop my academical English - both spoken and written - which I believe will help me in my future studies and career.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy, but it definitely takes some effort to get used to an entirely different education system.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Queensland specifically had a department for exchange students and study abroad that was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding affordable housing in Brisbane is not easy. I ended up paying way more than I expected. If it hadn't been for my parents' support I would not have been able to afford it.
There are not really any recommendations as Australia has a housing crisis and your rights and priveleges as a student from abroad are very poor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It will probably be very expensive. I paid 8600 DKK per month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UQ's system is fairly easy and intuitive compared to other universities I imagine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail support and FAQ's

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went smoothly - 100% successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to read about the courses, their prerequisites, the timetables and their assesments and examinations. I had to change two of my subjects as I did not qualify for them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had two second year courses, one third year course and one that was mixed BA and MA students.
Beware, in Australia the difference between second and third year courses can be very significant in terms of assesments and hours spent each weak, so I do not recommend getting third year courses only.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar however, you feel more independent at UCPH. More of the classes at UQ were compulsory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Aquatic Environments
Food Chemistry
Chemical Biology
Experimental Pharmacology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Chemical Biology and Experimental Pharmacology were the hardest courses, but they also taught me a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than expected and food is very expensive in Australia

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and housing was more expensive.
Coffee is cheap though :D - and it is incredibly good!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Anything you can imagine is possible.
Some examples are kite-surfing, wake-bording, mountain-trekking, all sorts of sports, religious clubs, political clubs, social clubs, academical clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Social sports if you are into that. It is a good way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Noosa, Whitsundays, Byron Bay, Cairns, Great Barrier Reef.
There are so many incredibly beautiful spots in Queensland.
If you can afford it, go ahead and rent a car with some friends for the whole period - it will help you get around and experience Australia to the fullest.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as it is a western culture that is similar to that of Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Australians are very open and friendly so do not hesitate to go and talk to your local classmates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very open and laid back in Australia

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure you choose the right courses. They can be changed during the first couple of weeks so there is no rush. I recommend you choose something that you find interesting and do not burden yourself with four intense third year courses.
2. Make friends with the locals in your courses as they can really help you academically
3. Get a car with some friends if you can and take every chance you get to go out and explore Australia!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect of it. Getting to know so many new people from all around the world is amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Pushing yourself to be the most social and open person you can be in order to gain as many friendships as possible and experience as much as possible.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
